🔊 Islamabad hosts 10th meeting of Pakistan–Iran Joint Trade Committee

📌 Islamabad, IRNA — The 10th meeting of the Joint Trade Committee of the Islamic Republic of Iran and Pakistan has been scheduled in Islamabad with senior officials from both countries in attendance.

Senior officials from Iran and Pakistan are set to meet on Tuesday and Wednesday (4–5 August) for the next round of Joint Trade Committee discussions in the Pakistani capital.
​
Seyyed Mohammad Atabak, Iran’s Minister of Industry, Mine and Trade, is expected to travel to Islamabad at the head of a delegation to attend the 10th meeting of the committee.
​
The committee meeting is expected to discuss key priorities such as progress on a free trade agreement, more facilitated transit operations, and stronger border infrastructure between Iran and Pakistan.

🖥 Israel launches new attacks on southern Lebanon in violation of truce

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Israeli regime has continued its attacks on southern Lebanon, targeting several areas with drones and artillery despite a ceasefire between the two sides.

According to reports from Lebanon on Monday, the latest Israeli attacks targeted neighborhoods in the cities of Tyre, Marjayoun, and Bint Jbeil, as well as surrounding villages. Israeli drones also carried out bombing runs over the Ali al-Taher Heights in Nabatiyeh, dropping explosive and incendiary munitions.
​
In the village of Chamaa, near Tyre, the Israeli military fired artillery shells, while troops set fire to olive groves in the villages of Tayibe and Yaroun.
​
Fighting resumed between Israel and Lebanon on March 2, when the Hezbollah resistance movement launched attacks on Israel in retaliation for the regime’s near-daily strikes on Lebanon and the assassination of Iran’s Leader Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei two days earlier.
​
Israel subsequently launched a ground invasion and occupied parts of southern Lebanon. On April 16, Israel and Lebanon agreed to a ceasefire, but the truce has been repeatedly violated.
​
On June 26, the two sides signed a framework agreement brokered by the United States in Washington. Under the framework, Israeli troops are to withdraw from southern Lebanon and be replaced by units of the Lebanese Armed Forces.
​
Hezbollah Secretary General Sheikh Naeem Qassem described the framework as a surrender to Israel. Critics also pointed to the absence of a specific timetable for the withdrawal of Israeli forces.
